note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after d6e44c3bb1). Section 4.4.1: "Since the SPD-I is just a part of the SPD, if a packet that is looked up in the SPD-I cannot be matched to an entry there, then the packet MUST be discarded." The only cited producer that moved is warnSPDLeft (spd_left.go): d6e44c3bb1 changed the warning text alone (each leftover entry is now named by its full `ip xfrm policy delete` command via describe/deleteCommand, sorted, carrying proto, sport, dport and if_id). Its contract is unchanged: it returns true exactly when the ledger is non-empty, and releaseSPD (apply.go) still returns before removeUnmatched in that case, so the catch-all still outlives every Ze entry a removal left. The gap paths are unaffected: VPP runs only under `unmatched bypass` with no catch-all (vppPolicyInterface, CatchAllSupported answering ErrNoNodeWideSPD), and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 manual-key entries installed via defaultDataplaneSource have no catch-all beneath them, so an inbound packet can still meet no SPD-I entry and be delivered. Named tests TestReleaseSPDKeepsTheCatchAllWhenARemovalFails (now asserting the command form), TestRFC4301FinalEntryIsUnderEveryZeSPDEntry, TestRunInstallsNoSPDEntryBeforeTheFirstApply, TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketMatchingNoEntryFollowsTheUnmatchedLeaf and TestUnmatched* pass at HEAD. Gap stands; {gap} annotation accurate.
